The test blade had one row of film cooling holes near the suction side gill hole region.
The film cooling holes had a diameter of 1.91 mm and a length-to-diameter ratio (L/D) of 7.9.
The lateral expansion angle of the fanshaped and laidback fanshaped holes was 7.24°.
The forward expansion angle of the laidback fanshaped holes was 25°.
The mainstream Reynolds number based on cascade exit velocity was 5.3x10^5.
The average uncertainty in the heat transfer coefficient measurement was ±6.5%.
The uncertainty in the film cooling effectiveness measurement was about 9.2%.
The uncertainty in the coolant jet temperature field measurements was 5.8% using the cold-wire and less than 1% using the thermocouple.
For the fanshaped holes, film effectiveness initially decreased with increasing blowing ratio, but then increased again at the highest blowing ratio of 1.2.
For the laidback fanshaped holes, film effectiveness increased monotonically with increasing blowing ratio.

The unsteady wake generally reduced film effectiveness downstream of the film cooling holes, except for the case of the fanshaped holes at the highest blowing ratio of 1.2, where the unsteady wake increased film effectiveness in the front region.

The coolant jet temperature field for the cylindrical holes was measured using a cold-wire system, while for the fanshaped and laidback fanshaped holes, it was measured using a traversing fine-gage thermocouple probe.
The transient liquid crystal technique was used to measure the detailed heat transfer coefficients and film cooling effectiveness on the blade suction surface.
The blade had an axial chord length of 17 cm and a radial span of 25.2 cm.
The blade spacing at the cascade inlet was 17.01 cm, and the throat-to-blade span ratio was 0.2.
